gold.reasoning: 1. Rocky Mountain spotted fever was later excluded because the rash was salmon colored and worsened with fever spikes — “We feel that our patient's symptoms were not due to RMSF, because the rash was salmon colored and worsened with the fever spikes.” 2. Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia infections were ruled out by negative serologies — “Serology for Mycoplasma and Chlamydia was negative.” 3. Adult-onset Still’s disease was diagnosed based on fulfillment of clinical criteria — “Our patient's current symptoms were consistent with Yamaguchi criteria for Adult Onset Still's disease.”

source_issues: s005: the reason for the current metronidazole is not given.
The gold reasoning says the rash worsened with fever spikes; the prompt only says the rash appeared almost at the same time as the fevers.
notes: Index visit: the presentation (admission) after 2 weeks of joint and muscle pains and a week of daily fevers, rash, sore throat, nausea and vomiting (s001-s011); laboratory, serology and CT results (s012-s018) are findings from the same admission.
s001 and s002: location and duration shared by several symptoms are standalone facts (f003, f004, f015).
Conjunctival injection, cervical lymphadenopathy, abdominal tenderness and the enlarged spleen are examiner findings; the patient does not report them, so they are not facts.
Gold-diagnosis words (adult, onset, still) are avoided in fact items and texts; f011 uses the item 'rash: when it appeared' for that reason.
